payload.question: How much of the council's money comes from renting out commercial property?
payload.label: Commercial property and lending as a share of core funding, 2024/25
payload.council_caveat: Two cautions the council's own table makes clear. It added a notional £1.755m of borrowing cost for properties bought between 2017 and 2020 into the later years, and the figure it divides by grew from £21.4m to £29.0m over the same period. Both push the percentage down without anything changing on the ground.
payload.evidence: The council publishes its own indicator for this: net commercial income as a percentage of net revenue stream. It was 16% in 2021/22 and 4% in 2024/25. There is no target to judge it against — the council has not published one — so this is a number, not a score.
